about: The upload workbook: every tab and column. page/workbook.py reads uploads and makes the empty sheet from this file only. See the root CLAUDE.md > The upload sheet.

lines: Upload sheet: how to fill it
Organization Customers = Oracle's Create Organization Customer screen. Person Customers = Create Person Customer screen.
Order Types: one row per order type, as on Oracle's Manage Order Lookups screen. Row 4 is a sample.

Payment Terms: one row per term on Payment Terms, its installments on Payment Term Lines (in order) and its sets on Payment Term Sets. Lines and sets name their term in Payment Term Name, written exactly as the Name (capitals and spaces count).

Lookup Types: one row per NEW lookup type on Lookup Types (always a User type; type names in capitals, not starting with ORA). Its codes go on Lookup Codes, joined by Lookup Type written exactly (capitals and spaces count).

A code row whose Lookup Type is not on the Lookup Types tab adds that code to a lookup type that already exists in Oracle (User or Extensible types; System types can't get codes). Existing types and codes are never changed.
One bad code makes Oracle drop its WHOLE lookup type (the other types are saved); a rerun creates only what is missing.

Business Units: one row per business unit, as on Oracle's Create Business Unit screen (Name, Active, Location, Manager, Default Set). Order Manager and Pricing Administrator access on it for the configured user is added automatically; there is no column for it.

Business functions, ledger, legal entity, currency, profit center, service providers and set assignments are not created. An existing business unit is never changed; only missing access is added to it.

A name that differs from an existing business unit only in capitals (abd / ABD) is the same business unit for Oracle: that row is skipped and never sent. Manager: only Yaqub, Younas or Smith, Aron. Empty Location or Manager = none.

Price Lists: one row per price list (header only: no items, charges or tiers yet), as on Oracle's Create Price List screen; it is approved once its access sets are added. Price List Access Sets: one row per access set, joined by Price List Name written exactly (capitals and spaces count); every price list needs at least one.
Price list names are unique across ALL of Oracle (not per business unit), and capitals count: 'abc' next to an existing 'ABC' would be a NEW price list. An existing name is skipped and never changed.

A price list's Business Unit may also be one on the Business Units tab of this sheet: business units are created first, and the price list waits until Oracle shows that business unit for pricing. Dates: YYYY-MM-DD; Oracle shows them at 12:00 AM in the Oracle user's time zone.
Yellow headers (*) are required. Blue are optional; empty means Oracle's default.
Customers tabs: up to 100 customers per upload. A kind of setup whose tabs are empty is simply not created.
Address Purposes: one row per purpose. Customer Name = the customer's Name (organization) or First Name + space + Last Name (person).
Not in the sheet (Oracle fills them): Registry ID, Account Number, Site Number, Site on a purpose.
Dates are text, YYYY-MM-DD. Purpose dates must be within the address dates.
Test environment only. Delete the dummy rows before a real upload.

readme_areas.about: Read me lines of an area's own blank sheet (the page's Order Management | Receivables switch, 2026-10-30); the full sheet and the Order Management sheet use "readme" above.
Receivables: Receivables Payment Terms: one row per term, as on Oracle's Manage Receivables Payment Terms screen. Its installments go on Receivables Term Lines (in order), joined by Payment Term Name written exactly as the Name (capitals and spaces count).
Name: at most 15 characters. A term whose Name and Set Code are already in Oracle is skipped and never changed. Set Code is never filled in for you.
Relative Amount is each installment's share of the Base Amount (empty Base Amount = 100, so the installments are percentages); together they must equal the Base Amount exactly.
Each installment: ONE of Days, Fixed Date or Day of Month (Day of Month needs Months Ahead; 0 = same month). Up to three discounts, each with its own percent and one date.
With 2 or more installments, Print Lead Days (a whole number above 0) and Tax and Freight are required. With a discount, Discount Basis is required (Invoice amount or Lines only for now).
Not in the sheet (always the create default): In Use No, Allow Discount on Partial Payments No, no billing cycle, flexfields, other languages (the name is written in Oracle's one base language).

AutoInvoice Grouping Rules: one row per rule, as on Oracle's Manage AutoInvoice Grouping Rules screen (Name at most 40 characters, not starting with ORA_; From Date is required and never filled in for you). An existing name is skipped and never changed.

Grouping Rule Classes: one row per transaction class of a rule (Invoice, Debit Memo, Credit Memo), joined by Grouping Rule Name written exactly. To group a class also by a characteristic, fill Characteristic; one row per characteristic, the same class repeated. A characteristic must already be used by a grouping rule in Oracle.
Not in the sheet: line ordering rule, flexfields, consolidated billing.

Transaction Types: one row per type, as on Oracle's Manage Transaction Types screen, header only (Name at most 20 characters; Item Description at most 80). Every column with * must be filled: nothing is filled in for you. An existing Name in the same set is skipped.

Only Invoice and Debit Memo, with Creation Sign Positive Sign and Transaction Status Open, are offered for now. Accounts (receivable, revenue, tax, freight and the other account fields, per business unit) are not offered yet: they can create new account combinations in the general ledger.

A Payment Term needs its Payment Term Set. When the term is a Name on the Receivables Payment Terms tab, that term is created first and the type waits for it (not sent if the term failed or was skipped); otherwise it must already be in Oracle in that set.

Transaction Sources: one row per source, as on Oracle's Manage Transaction Sources screen (Name not starting with ORA_, Set Code, Item Description and From Date required; Last Number required with automatic numbering, and the numbering starts there). An existing Name in the same set is skipped.

A Grouping Rule only applies to an Imported source. When it is a Name on the AutoInvoice Grouping Rules tab, that rule is created first and the source waits for it (not sent if the rule failed or was skipped); otherwise it must already be in Oracle.
Yellow headers (*) are required. Blue are optional; empty means the default shown in the hint.
Test environment only. Delete the dummy rows before a real upload.
